items.q: How many liters of water are in the tank at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> minutes?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>51.891</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">51.891</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.891</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.891</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>93.891</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93.891</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>55.212</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55.212</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: The amount is the starting amount plus the net change: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>6</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50 + \int_0^6 \left(r(t) - 7\right)dt</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>51.891</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 51.891</annotation></semantics></math> liters. Store the integral in the calculator and round only at the end.
options: The 50 liters at the start plus the net change, the integral of the rate in minus the rate out.

This is the net change alone; the 50 liters already in the tank at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> are left out.
This adds all the water that flowed in but never subtracts the 7 liters per minute that drain out.

This is the amount at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.807</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 4.807</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(t) = 7</annotation></semantics></math>, not at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At what time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 6</annotation></semantics></math>, is the amount of water in the tank greatest?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.422</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.422</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.807</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.807</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: The amount <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(t)</annotation></semantics></math> has <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A'(t) = r(t) - 7</annotation></semantics></math>, which is 0 at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.422</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 1.422</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.807</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 4.807</annotation></semantics></math>. Compare <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> at these and the endpoints: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(0) = 50</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.422</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>49.055</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(1.422) \approx 49.055</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4.807</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>55.212</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(4.807) \approx 55.212</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>51.891</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(6) \approx 51.891</annotation></semantics></math>. The greatest is at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.807</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 4.807</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> the tank holds 50 liters, but the amount later climbs above that.

Here <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(t) - 7</annotation></semantics></math> changes from negative to positive, so the amount has its least value near this time, not its greatest.

Here <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(t) - 7</annotation></semantics></math> changes from positive to negative, and the candidates test shows <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>55.212</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A \approx 55.212</annotation></semantics></math> liters beats both endpoints.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> the tank holds about 51.891 liters, less than at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.807</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 4.807</annotation></semantics></math>, because water drains out faster than it flows in after that time.

items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>, with its units?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.665</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.665</annotation></semantics></math> liters per minute per minute

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.665</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.665</annotation></semantics></math> liters per minute
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.637</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.637</annotation></semantics></math> liters per minute per minute
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.909</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.909</annotation></semantics></math> liters per minute per minute

why.correct: With the calculator's numerical derivative, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.665</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r'(4) \approx -1.665</annotation></semantics></math>. The rate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is in liters per minute, so its rate of change is in liters per minute per minute: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math> the inflow rate is falling.
options: The numerical derivative at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, in the units of a rate of a rate.
The value is right, but a derivative of a rate in liters per minute has units of liters per minute per minute.

This is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(4)</annotation></semantics></math>, the inflow rate itself, not how fast it is changing.

This is the average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, not the rate at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = e^x - x^2</annotation></semantics></math>. At what value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the interval <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 2)</annotation></semantics></math> is the instantaneous rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> equal to the average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2]</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.370</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.370</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.195</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.195</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.693</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.693</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: The average rate of change is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(2) - f(0)}{2 - 0}</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{e^2 - 5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.195</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 1.195</annotation></semantics></math>. Solve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = e^x - 2x = \frac{e^2 - 5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> with the calculator: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.370</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 1.370</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The solution of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x - 2x = \frac{e^2 - 5}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is the average rate of change itself, a slope, not the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> where the slope of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> matches it.

This is where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = e^x - 2x</annotation></semantics></math> is least, not where it equals the average rate of change.

This is the midpoint of the interval; the derivative there is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e - 2</annotation></semantics></math>, not the average rate of change.

items.q: A particle moves along a line with velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = 2\cos(0.8t) - 0.3t</annotation></semantics></math>. Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, and why?
options: Speeding up, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.375</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(3) \approx -2.375</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.381</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(3) \approx -1.381</annotation></semantics></math> have the same sign

Slowing down, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.381</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(3) \approx -1.381</annotation></semantics></math> is negative

Slowing down, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.375</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(3) \approx -2.375</annotation></semantics></math> is negative

Speeding up, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(3)</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\cos(2.4) - 0.9</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2.375</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx -2.375</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.381</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(3) = v'(3) \approx -1.381</annotation></semantics></math> (radian mode). Both are negative, so the speed is increasing: the particle moves left faster and faster.
options: Speeding up needs the signs of both <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, and here they agree.
A negative acceleration alone does not mean slowing down; with a negative velocity it means speeding up.
A negative velocity tells the direction (left), not whether the speed grows.

The conclusion is right, but the reason is not: a decreasing velocity is a negative acceleration, which says nothing about speed until it is compared with the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The derivative of a function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = e^{\sin x} - 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>. At what value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the interval <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 4)</annotation></semantics></math> does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> have a relative maximum?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.417</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.417</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.724</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.724</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.571</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.571</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.142</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.142</annotation></semantics></math>

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = \ln 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.417</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 0.417</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.724</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 2.724</annotation></semantics></math>. Between them <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f' > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and after <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.724</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 2.724</annotation></semantics></math> it is negative, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> changes from positive to negative there: a relative maximum.

items.q: People enter a park at the rate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1200</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(t) = 1200e^{-(t - 3)^2/2}</annotation></semantics></math> people per hour, for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 8</annotation></semantics></math> hours. why.correct: The number entering is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^8 E(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>3003.893</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3003.893</annotation></semantics></math>, about 3004 people.
options: The integral of the rate over the 8 hours.

This is the average rate, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{8}\int_0^8 E(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, in people per hour, not a number of people.
This is the greatest rate, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, not an amount.
This multiplies the greatest rate by 8 hours, as if the rate stayed at its peak.
